source.title: AdamNX: An Adam improvement algorithm based on a novel exponential decay mechanism for the second-order moment estimate
source.authors: Meng Zhu; Quan Xiao; Wei-Dong Min

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It notes that a recurrence's mathematical correctness remains subject to author verification.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on held-out image-classification error using reported configurations, bearing on V4 with a different optimizer and evaluation setup. It does not measure the training-to-test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on visual tasks. Only the CIFAR-100 image-classification results in Tables 11 and 12 bear on V4. Other task results and coefficient ablations do not measure V4's optimizer comparison. The paper says it reports single results and uses no systematic tuning or multi-seed statistics.
record.test_reason: Tables 11–12 compare held-out image-classification error under momentum SGD and alternative optimizers, including adaptive methods. These results bear on V4, although optimizer-specific learning rates and weight decay differ, systematic tuning was absent, and training performance is not compared.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors propose AdamNX, describe an assumption-dependent trend toward momentum-SGD-like updates, and restrict empirical conclusions to the reported visual-task configurations. They explicitly do not establish statistical significance, flatness, cross-task generalization, convergence rates, general stability, or engineering overhead; recurrence correctness remains subject to author verification.
record.recipe_differences: Uses AdamNX, a time-varying second-moment decay optimizer, and compares it with several optimizers under the paper's reported configurations; no systematic tuning or multi-seed statistics.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparison changes across model architectures and optimizer configurations; the paper states that systematic tuning was not used.

fits_no_version.finding: Comparisons among Adam, AdaX, AdamNX, and second-moment coefficient variants report classification, detection, segmentation, and convergence results without an SGD comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the second-moment decay schedule can improve reported task performance relative to other adaptive configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: The analytic mechanism makes late-stage updates approach momentum-SGD-like behavior under stated assumptions, without establishing flatness or generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A time-varying second-moment coefficient can weaken adaptive update scaling during training.

record.problems: Single reported results; no multi-seed means, standard deviations, significance tests, or unified tuning budget. Optimizer-specific learning rates and weight decay differ, and the paper says systematic tuning was not used. The results give test error but no training error, so they do not measure the generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: Other optimizer metrics in Tables 11 and 12 (Top-5 error) were omitted because the Top-1 metric already records the same optimizer comparison and the tables do not present Top-5 as a disagreeing metric. CIFAR-100 comparisons in Tables 3–4 and ablations in Tables 7–8 compare adaptive optimizers, not adaptive methods against SGD, so they do not bear directly on V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks; equal or better training performance despite worse held-out performance; controlled learning-rate-only tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay comparisons; and explicit Adam-to-SGD switching.
Batch-size effects and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout comparisons, small-data regimes, and removing dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: SophiaG's Top-5 error is 15.42% versus momentum SGD's 16.19% on EfficientNetV2-L, reversing their Top-1 ordering. Although Top-5 omissions were declared, the record incorrectly says they contain no disagreeing comparison; this result needs a row.

record.verdict_notes: All tabulated Top-1 values are transcribed correctly. The record's EfficientNetV2-L disadvantage group supports V4 rather than merely limiting it. Counterexamples qualify the empirical tendency; they do not refute an 'often' claim universally. Single runs, differing weight decay, and no unified tuning budget restrict interpretation. No training-versus-test gap is established.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label versus random-label comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No language benchmarks, broad optimizer tuning, Adam-to-SGD switching, decoupled weight decay comparison, or training-error comparison.
